paragraphs: One-line judgment: Automotive Glass Installers and Repairers are not "automotive service technicians" but a work position that replaces or repairs motor vehicle windshields and window glass: removing the broken glass, cleaning and preparing the bonding surfaces, applying primer and polyurethane adhesive, installing and reinstalling trim, wipers, and other fittings, waiting for the cure according to temperature and humidity, and inspecting the seal and appearance; people who only want to fit a ready-made part and are unwilling to take responsibility for bonding surface preparation and curing conditions are not suited to it.

Signals to keep exploring: you can select tools, safety protection, and fittings as required, are willing to clean and prepare bonding surfaces per procedure and to control the evenness and thickness of the primer and adhesive, are willing to judge the curing time by temperature and humidity and to check fitting reinstallation item by item, and can stop and verify when the glass model or the bonding surface condition is unclear.

Conditions for pausing your investment: you have not yet completed one full disassembly—cleaning—bonding—reinstallation—inspection loop under any supervised conditions, or you can only describe your interest as "liking cars"; also do not treat being able to drive or being able to take parts apart as proof that you can independently handle structural glass and safety part reinstallation. Work involving glass safety performance and vehicle structural and airbag-related areas must be carried out per the applicable standards and institutional processes and must leave a traceable basis; this page does not provide installation, repair, or field work instructions.

Education and authorization must be verified separately: O*NET lists 49-3022.00 as Job Zone 1–2 (SVP below 6.0), and among the education levels published on the page 90% is requiring a high school diploma or equivalent, 9% is requiring less than a high school diploma, and 1% is requiring a postsecondary certificate; the BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook lists the typical entry-level education for the body and glass repair chapter as a high school diploma or equivalent, with no related work experience and no on-the-job training required, and also notes that industry certification is becoming increasingly important. On the mainland China side, "automotive glass installer" is not listed separately in the Occupational Classification Code (2022 edition), and the related work falls under the class three special repair items of motor vehicle repair (including automotive glass installation and repair); safety glass is a product subject to mandatory national standard management. Education, vendor or industry certification, institutional authorization to work and work authorization, the special operations certificate, and product certification approval are different statuses and must be verified item by item according to employer, position, and location.

One line: this is a work position that safely replaces or repairs broken glass and is responsible for bonding and curing quality; the core is disassembly and cleaning, bonding surface preparation and sealing, fitting reinstallation and inspection, and recording and handover per procedure, rather than an interest in cars or experience with driving.

The work of Automotive Glass Installers and Repairers falls into three categories: disassembly and replacement (removing the broken windshield or window glass from the vehicle and removing the frame screws fixing the glass with tools; obtaining the windshield or window from stock by vehicle model, checking it for defects, and installing it; applying foam spacers on the pinchweld; installing rubber channel strips on the edge of the glass or frame to prevent water leaks or noise; replacing or adjusting power or manual window regulator mechanisms; and cutting flat safety glass to a template or doing precision layout and glass cutting for custom replacement windows, and shaping and smoothing cut or uneven edges against an automatic sanding belt); bonding surface preparation and sealing (removing all dirt, foreign material, and loose glass from the damaged area, applying primer along the windshield or window edge and letting it dry; applying primer to scratches on the pinchweld and letting it dry; checking for and removing moisture or contamination from the damaged area and keeping it dry until the repair is complete; applying a bead of polyurethane adhesive around the perimeter of each pinchweld and working the excess adhesive to an even thickness; allowing enough cure time for polyurethane-installed glass according to temperature and humidity; and cooling or warming the glass at temperature extremes); and reinstallation and inspection (replacing or reinstalling previously removed trim, clips, wipers, and other parts; installing or repairing safety glass and related materials, such as rear window defroster elements; and selecting the appropriate tools, safety protection, and fittings as required by the work). All three categories presuppose stopping and verifying when the glass model, the bonding surface condition, or the curing conditions are unclear.

The U.S. O*NET49-3022.00 definition is replacing or repairing motor vehicle windshield and window glass. The original tasks include disassembly and installation, bonding surface cleaning and priming, adhesive application, curing by temperature and humidity, fitting reinstallation, window regulator mechanisms, and cutting and shaping safety glass; not every position performs all of them. The O*NET details list 18 tasks (15 Core, 3 Supplemental) and 41 work activities and publish Importance scores: selecting tools, protection, and fittings 88, two primer preparation items 85, removing moisture and contamination 83, applying polyurethane 82; general physical activity 81, handling and moving objects 77, getting information 61, and direct public service 60. The scores are occupational group importance, not frequency or an individual threshold.

entries: Vehicle intake and confirmation | Make the object and requirements clear | Verify the vehicle model and glass model, confirm the damage type and the repairable scope, record pre-existing vehicle damage and inform the owner, and mark the steps that need authorization.

Disassembly and installation work | Keep the operation controllable | Use tools to remove the broken glass and trim and clips and wipers, protect the surrounding paint and interior, and obtain and inspect the replacement glass by vehicle model.

Bonding surface preparation and sealing | Make the bond reliable | Remove dirt and foreign material and loose glass, handle moisture and contamination and keep the surface dry, apply primer, and apply adhesive per procedure and work it to an even thickness.

Curing and reinstallation | Make the result reviewable | Allow enough cure time according to temperature and humidity, reinstall trim and clips and wipers and other parts, and replace or adjust the window regulator mechanism when necessary.

Inspection and records | Make the process traceable | Inspect the seal and appearance and fitting function, and record the vehicle model and glass model, the handling process, quantities used, curing conditions, and inspection results.

Collaboration and handover | Make responsibility attributable | Coordinate with the front desk and supervisors and parts management, and report open items honestly; matters involving structural parts and safety parts and product certification follow the authorized process.

Work environment | 98% wear routine protective or safety equipment every day, 95% need face-to-face discussions every day, 89% talk on the telephone every day, 84% are exposed outdoors to various weather every day, 84% are inside enclosed vehicles or operating enclosed equipment every day, 79% face time pressure every day, 23% are exposed to extreme heat or cold every day, 59% are in overly bright or poorly lit conditions weekly but not daily, and 38% are exposed to distracting or uncomfortable noise monthly but not weekly.
Main equipment and tools | Glass suction cups and lifting tools, cutting and shaping tools (such as an automatic sanding belt), primer and polyurethane adhesive and application tools, trim and clip removal tools, window regulator mechanism removal tools, and personal protection (gloves, safety glasses, cut-resistant gear).
Task rhythm | 66% have a 40-hour work week; 40% stand more than half the time, 26% use their hands to handle or control objects and tools more than half the time, 27% perform repetitive motions more than half the time, and 20% bend or twist their body less than half the time.
Collaboration | Work with vehicle owners and front desk reception, workshop supervisors, and parts and inventory management personnel; 43% consider dealing with external customers or the public very important, 36% consider cooperation with the work group or team important, and 29% spend most of their time in contact with others.
Competition and pressure | 29% consider the consequences of errors very serious, 33% consider their decisions very important to colleague or company results, 46% have limited decision freedom, 40% have some freedom over tasks and priorities and goals, and 25% never make decisions on their own.
Compliance and safety | Disassembly and bonding work must meet the applicable safety and environmental requirements; the GB9656-2021 official metadata status is current, released 2021-04-30 and effective 2023-01-01, and it is a mandatory standard for motor vehicle glass; this round did not obtain the full standard text and cannot claim, on the basis of a catalog description, that all indicators have been verified or use it as installation steps. Safety education and waste management for repair operators are covered by Articles 23/24 of the repair provisions; the specific tools, chemical SDS, and stop and recovery procedures should be verified separately. Mainland China's Provisions on the Administration of Motor Vehicle Repair, 2023 Order No. 14 amendment: operators file with the county-level competent transport department after business registration and repair according to the filed items; the class three special items include automotive glass installation and repair, and class one and two may also undertake special items, so it is not limited to class three. Article 30 requires recording the source of parts and prohibits counterfeit and substandard parts, allows equivalent parts that meet the conditions, and requires parts replaced to be handed to the repair client for their own handling. Article 33 requires a repair electronic file uploaded to the national motor vehicle repair health record system, so all materials cannot be summarized as prohibited from external transmission; individual authorization, data access, and specific operations must still follow the actual rules.
Records and review | The vehicle model and glass model, damage judgment, bonding surface preparation and curing conditions, and fitting reinstallation and inspection results need to be traceable; 13% consider precision or accuracy quite important, and 27% consider repeating the same task important.
Skills and training | O*NET lists this occupation as Job Zone 1–2 (SVP below 6.0); the basic skills list speaking, the cross-functional skills list installation and equipment selection; knowledge is mainly customer and personal service, mechanical, English language, and administration and management; abilities include near vision, manual dexterity, multi-limb coordination, static strength, arm-hand steadiness, and control precision (the details publish Importance: Speaking50, Installation53, Equipment Selection50, knowledge customer service 77, mechanical 68, English language 59, administration and management 50).
Entry and authorization | Education does not equal work authorization, and industry or vendor certification does not mean you can handle structural glass and safety part reinstallation in any setting; work must follow institutional processes and the applicable standards.
Industry and employers | The current O*NET broad industry distribution is other services (except public administration) 80% and other industries 20%, source year 2025; the BLS OOH lists, for this occupation's detailed industry, automotive body, paint, interior, and glass repair 77%, self-employed 10%, and construction 2%. The two classification levels differ, and the 20% is not all treated as retail nor the whole-chapter body data as this occupation. Mobile service is explicitly mentioned in the OOH; brand, chain, and accident vehicle scenarios serve as editorial comparison scenarios, and specific recruiting was not verified.
Education, training, and licensure | The O*NET survey asks what education new hires need: 90% answer high school or equivalent, 9% below high school, and 1% postsecondary certificate, which is not the incumbent education composition. Zone1—2/SVP<6.0 is a preparation-level description, with some requiring little experience and some several months to a year, not a fixed number of years for all positions. The BLS EP typical entry for this occupation is a high school diploma, related experience None, and moderate-term on-the-job training; None does not prohibit prior experience, and training is not none. The OOH notes that the basic glass worker skills can be learned in 6 months or more and full independence usually requires training of up to 1 year; the 2—3 years for body workers cannot be transferred. The U.S. BLS suggests checking state requirements: a few states require licensing for automotive glass installers and repairers; industry certification and state licensure are different. The AGSC examination conditions page requires a Master to have at least 3 years of industry experience and to first pass the Technician examination; the Certified/Qualified designation depends on whether the company is an AGSC member, and the designation changes accordingly when moving to a non-member company. What was actually read is the examination eligibility and designation rules, not a uniform practical examination, all-state licensure, or independent work authorization.
Safe drive-away time and corrosion | AGSC explains that the minimum drive-away time depends on the adhesive type and brand and the atmospheric conditions at the time, and the vehicle should remain stationary until that time has elapsed; corrosion may interfere with the bond between the glass and the body, and corrosion affecting installation must be treated first, with referral to a professional when necessary. This is North American industry safety guidance, not the complete per-model procedures or Chinese regulations obtained this round.

Work with vehicle owners and front desk reception, workshop supervisors, parts and inventory management personnel, and body repair and mechanical and electrical repair positions; when glass safety performance, vehicle structural and airbag-related areas, and sealing and drainage requirements are involved, follow the applicable standards and institutional procedures, do not decide on your own, and stop and escalate when the basis is unclear.

Automotive Glass Installers and Repairers focus on the disassembly, installation, repair, and sealing of windshields and window glass and are responsible for bonding surface preparation and curing conditions; automotive body and glass repairers focus on body sheet metal and painting and also handle glass; glass installers (architectural glass) focus on architectural and decorative glass, with buildings rather than vehicles as the object; automotive service technicians and mechanics focus on mechanical and electrical system repair; tire repairers and changers focus on tires; automotive and watercraft service attendants focus on fueling and routine maintenance and sales; electric motor and power tool repairers focus on motors and power tools. Adjacent occupations share basic tools and safety knowledge, but the objects, deliverables, and responsibilities differ.
Installation and repair results that can be fitted, reinstalled, and reviewed

Complete disassembly, bonding, and reinstallation per procedure, and leave a work record stating the vehicle model and glass model, the bonding surface preparation process, the primer and adhesive used, the curing conditions and time, the fitting reinstallation and inspection results, and the parts that remain uncertain, so that the supervisor or quality inspection personnel can judge from it.
Installation work orders and inspection records

The objects are motor vehicle windshields and window glass and their related materials (rear window defroster elements, trim, clips, wipers, window regulator mechanisms, channel strips, and foam spacers); the basis is the mandatory national standard, the vehicle manufacturer's repair information and work procedures, the institution's onboarding and quality inspection processes, and the instructions for parts and materials.

Automotive Glass Installers and Repairers (U.S. side O*NET 49-3022.00, Automotive Glass Installers and Repairers) replace or repair motor vehicle windshields and window glass. The original official duties read "Replace or repair broken windshields and window glass in motor vehicles."; O*NET lists 18 official tasks, focused on selecting the appropriate tools, safety protection, and fittings as required by the work; applying primer to scratches on the pinchweld and letting it dry; removing dirt, foreign material, and loose glass from the damaged area and applying primer along the edge and letting it dry; checking for and removing moisture or contamination from the damaged area and keeping it dry; applying a bead of polyurethane adhesive around the perimeter of each pinchweld and working the excess adhesive to an even thickness; obtaining the windshield or window from stock by vehicle model, checking it for defects, and installing it; installing or repairing safety glass and related materials such as rear window defroster elements; allowing enough cure time for polyurethane-installed glass according to temperature and humidity; replacing or reinstalling previously removed trim, clips, wipers, and other parts; removing the frame screws fixing the glass with tools to remove the broken glass; replacing or adjusting power or manual window regulator mechanisms; removing trim, clips, wipers, screws and bolts, A-pillar interior trim, and the headliner to prepare the work; installing new foam spacers on the pinchweld when necessary; installing rubber channel strips on the edge of the glass or frame to prevent water leaks or noise; cutting flat safety glass to a template or doing precision layout and custom cutting; shaping and smoothing cut or uneven edges against an automatic sanding belt; and cooling or warming the glass at temperature extremes. In the United States this occupation is in Job Zone 1–2 (SVP below 6.0); mainland China statistics are aggregated by industry category and job category and do not list this occupation separately, and the related work falls under the class three special repair items of motor vehicle repair. This page does not constitute installation, repair, or field work instructions, and the relevant decisions must be made by organizations and personnel with the appropriate qualifications and authorization following the applicable standards and processes.
Vehicle intake—disassembly—cleaning—bonding—reinstallation—inspection

Verify the vehicle model and glass model → remove the broken glass and protect the surrounding area → clean and prepare the bonding surfaces → apply primer and adhesive per procedure → install and reinstall the fittings → inspect the seal and appearance after curing.
Reviewable installation and inspection records

The vehicle model and glass model, the damage and repairable scope determination, bonding surface cleaning and drying, primer and adhesive quantities and evenness, curing temperature and humidity and time, the fitting reinstallation list, the inspection results, and the parts that remain uncertain.
The individual and the workshop supervisor (or quality inspection personnel)

Disassembly safety, bonding surface preparation and curing conditions, and the quality of sealing and fitting reinstallation are the individual's responsibility; matters involving vehicle structural and safety parts and product certification and recall are decided by organizations and personnel with the appropriate qualifications and authorization, and when the basis is unclear or the work is beyond the authorized scope, work must stop and be escalated.
Education and preparation

O*NET lists 49-3022.00 as Job Zone 1–2 (SVP below 6.0), typically requiring a high school diploma or equivalent, with some occupations possibly not requiring prior experience and job training ranging from a few days to a year; among the education levels published on the page, 90% is requiring a high school diploma or equivalent, 9% is requiring less than a high school diploma, and 1% is requiring a postsecondary certificate. The BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook lists the typical entry-level education for this chapter as a high school diploma or equivalent, with no related work experience and no on-the-job training required, and also notes that most employers prefer people who have completed body or glass repair training and that industry certification is becoming increasingly important. O*NET also lists the registered apprenticeship title "Glass Installer (Auto Serv)" and two industry certifications. On the mainland China side, training is mainly through motor vehicle repair related vocational skills training and mentoring by experienced workers, with specific requirements set by the employer.
Not interchangeable

Education, vendor or industry certification (such as the Auto Glass Safety Council's Certified Auto Glass Technician and Certified Auto Glass Master in the United States), registered apprenticeship experience, institutional authorization to work and work authorization, the special operations certificate, and product certification approval are different statuses: education does not bring work authorization, and certification does not mean you can independently handle structural glass and safety part reinstallation or carry out disassembly and bonding work in any setting.

Check at least six items before starting: the occupational definition and the employer entity (O*NET 49-3022.00 is a U.S. definition; on the mainland China side the position and the employer must be identified); education and professional training; the employer's internal authorization to work and the scope of work authorization; the work procedures for disassembly and bonding and inspection; the authenticity, source, and traceability requirements for glass and fittings; and the pay method (hourly wage, piece rate, or monthly salary plus commission).
Occupational definition

The U.S. side is O*NET 49-3022.00 (Automotive Glass Installers and Repairers); on the mainland China side you must first identify whether the position belongs to a brand-authorized service center, a chain glass replacement shop, a general auto repair shop, an accident vehicle repair center, or a mobile on-site replacement service, because different employers differ greatly in work procedures, quality inspection, and fitting source requirements.
Education and major pathways

On the U.S. side a high school diploma or equivalent predominates (among the education levels published on the O*NET page, 90% is requiring a high school diploma or equivalent), most employers prefer people who have completed body or glass repair training, and a registered apprenticeship title exists; on the mainland China side, training is mainly through motor vehicle repair related vocational skills training and mentoring by experienced workers, with specific education requirements set by the employer.
Authorization to work and work permits

Disassembly, bonding, and inspection must follow institutional processes and the applicable standards. On the U.S. side industry certification (the Auto Glass Safety Council's Certified Auto Glass Technician and Certified Auto Glass Master) is used to demonstrate specific abilities but does not equal institutional work authorization; on the mainland China side motor vehicle repair operations are subject to filing management, the class three special repair items include automotive glass installation and repair, repair parts must have a traceable source and counterfeit or substandard parts must not be used (Ministry of Transport, Provisions on the Administration of Motor Vehicle Repair, fifth amendment by Order No. 14 of 2023); safety glass is a product subject to mandatory national standard management. Before starting, verify pre-job training and work authorization and the quality inspection process; this cannot be inferred directly from education or certification.
Equipment and site safety

Disassembly work must meet the applicable safety requirements (protection against glass breakage and cuts, lifting and support and work-at-height protection, hand and power tool use, ventilation and personal protection for bonding materials and solvents, and waste disposal). The O*NET work context shows that 98% wear routine protective or safety equipment every day, 84% are exposed outdoors to various weather every day, 84% are inside enclosed vehicles or operating enclosed equipment every day, 26% are exposed to hazardous equipment at least once a month, and 15% are exposed to minor burns, cuts, bites, or stings at least once a month; the Safety Technical Specifications for Motor Vehicle Glass (GB 9656-2021) sets mandatory requirements for the vision safety, strength safety, breakage safety, and environmental durability of motor vehicle glass. This page does not constitute installation, repair, or field work instructions.
Shifts and working hours

The work context shows that 66% have a 40-hour work week, 79% face time pressure every day, 95% need face-to-face discussions every day, 89% talk on the telephone every day, and 33% consider their decisions very important to company results; mobile on-site replacement is common, and the work is affected by the owner's schedule and the weather. When comparing jobs, put the working-hours structure and the overtime and piece-rate or commission arrangements into the written terms.
Continuing training and review

Glass materials and bonding processes, defroster elements and window regulator mechanisms, and the disassembly requirements of different vehicle models update quickly (O*NET lists 2 hot technologies: Microsoft Windows and Workday software; plus repair record, enterprise resource planning, and estimating software), requiring ongoing continuing training and process and tool maintenance; before starting, confirm the training arrangements, work authorization, and quality inspection and rework review mechanisms.

Both share windshields and window glass as the object, but the work of body and glass repairers is mainly sheet metal and painting with glass only a part of it; automotive glass installers narrow the object to glass disassembly, installation, repair, and sealing.

entries.answer: There are three core categories of tasks: removing the broken windshield or window glass and related fittings, obtaining and inspecting the replacement glass by vehicle model, installing foam spacers on the pinchweld or rubber channel strips on the edge of the glass or frame when necessary, replacing or adjusting power or manual window regulator mechanisms, and cutting and shaping flat safety glass to a template; removing dirt and foreign material and loose glass from the damaged area, handling moisture and contamination and keeping it dry, applying primer and applying polyurethane adhesive around the perimeter of the pinchweld and working it to an even thickness, and allowing enough cure time according to temperature and humidity; and reinstalling trim and clips and wipers and other parts and inspecting the seal and appearance and fitting function. The U.S. side corresponds to O*NET 49-3022.00, whose official duties are to replace or repair motor vehicle windshields and window glass.
entries.question: What do automotive glass installers and repairers do every day?

entries.answer: Mainly glass breakage and cuts and punctures, fall and crushing risks from lifting and support and work at height and under the vehicle, compliance risk from external sharing of customer and vehicle information, health and environmental risks from adhesives and solvents and waste, untraceable disassembly and quantity and inspection records, and work beyond authorization and unclear work permits. The controls are executing to the applicable standards, confirming the bonding surface and curing conditions first, and recording honestly and accepting quality inspection review. This page does not provide installation, repair, or field work instructions.

entries.answer: The more explanatory signals are: being able to complete disassembly and cleaning and adhesive application and reinstallation per procedure and record honestly, being able to judge whether the bonding surface and curing conditions meet the requirements, and being able to check item by item against the inspection checklist and stop and escalate on anomalies or when beyond authorization; "liking cars" or "being able to drive" alone cannot settle it. The Holland interest code is RC (Realistic + Conventional), and a consistent interest only indicates that the direction is close.

The official materials also do not give an automation substitution rate or a job disappearance year for this occupation.

entries.answer: Confirmation of the vehicle model and glass model and damage scope, bonding surface cleaning and drying, primer and adhesive quantities and evenness, curing conditions and time judgment, fitting reinstallation and seal and appearance inspection, and work decisions involving structural and safety parts must all be undertaken by the individual together with authorized personnel according to institutional procedures; system output must first be marked as reference and can only enter formal work orders and inspection records after on-site verification and procedure confirmation and inspection.

subject.name: Automotive Glass Installers and Repairers
subject.summary: Automotive Glass Installers and Repairers replace or repair motor vehicle windshields and window glass: removing the broken glass and fittings, cleaning and preparing the bonding surfaces, applying primer and polyurethane adhesive, waiting for the cure according to temperature and humidity, and reinstalling trim, clips, wipers, and other parts, with the core being disassembly and installation, bonding, curing, and inspection. The U.S. side corresponds to O*NET 49-3022.00 (Automotive Glass Installers and Repairers), in Job Zone 1–2 (SVP below 6.0); mainland China statistics are aggregated by industry category and job category and do not list this occupation separately, the related work falls under the class three special repair items of motor vehicle repair, and the industry and job category proxies are shown separately and not combined into a salary range.
